newsitem.title: USA: GM plant in Indiana hit by UAW strike.
newsitem.headline: GM plant in Indiana hit by UAW strike.

text.p: Some 2,700 United Auto Workers union members walked off the job at a General Motors Corp. plant in Ft. Wayne, Ind., Friday morning after all-night negotiations failed to reach agreement on a new contract.
"All I know is they're on strike," said a woman who answered the phone at UAW Local 2209's offices.
Negotiators talked through the night but were unable to reach an agreement on a new three year-contract, another union spokesman said.
The plant makes regular cab Chevrolet C/K and GMC Sierra full-size pickup trucks, turning out about 1,000 a day.
The UAW wants GM to hire more workers at the plant to cut down on overtime. The union also wants the company to address health and safety issues.
The walkout was the first strike over local contract terms since GM and the UAW reached a national agreement on a new three-year pact last November.
GM has local agreements with about 60 percent of its 105 UAW locals around the country.
The Ft. Wayne facility is the only one of GM's light truck plants that makes just regular cab full-size pickup trucks, which tend to be less popular than extended cab models.
